answer.rationale: Finance's 18% cost-cut mandate makes incumbent renewal alone insufficient unless paired with aggressive renegotiation. Memory c2 records that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor delivered a sharp unit-cost cut with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — directly aligned with the primary objective of minimizing TCO. However, the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and the contract expires in 14 days, so delivery risk is the binding constraint. Therefore, switching primary now should be combined with retaining a second-source tie-in (per c3 logic) to avoid single-point-of-failure exposure during the transition. c4 supports that benchmarking against market rates moves incumbents on price and terms, giving a credible walk-away position during any transition handoff. Verifying c2 and c4 first to confirm the cost-magnitude claim and the negotiation lever before committing.
